name: USCG Safety Drill
source: KB: squid-emergency-procedures / 46 CFR 185-25 + squid-on-board-binder quarterly drill schedule
intro: Log a USCG required safety drill. Per 46 CFR 185-25, drills must be performed quarterly. MOB, Abandon Ship, and Fire are required every quarter. Flooding at least once per year (Q1). Heart Attack/Medical at least once per year (Q2).

items.label: MOB: Announced location, eyes on person, life ring thrown, maneuvered to pick up, swim platform deployed

help.title: MOB Procedure (9 steps)
help.body:
1. Loudly announce 'Man Overboard' and location
2. Ensure multiple crew have eyes on person
3. Throw life ring
4. Maneuver vessel to pick up person
5. Crew member dons PFD, stands by swim platform
6. On captain's command, deploy swim platform, pull person aboard
7. Check health and breathing
8. If not located, notify Coast Guard
9. Continue search until released by Coast Guard

items.label: Fire: Moved passengers, donned lifejackets, cut fuel/electrical, used Class B extinguisher, did NOT open sealed spaces

help.title: Fire at Sea Procedure
help.body:
Phase 1: Move passengers, don lifejackets, VHF Ch 16, prepare to abandon
Phase 2: Cut fuel, kill electrical, close air supply, use Class B extinguisher. Do NOT open sealed machine space or hull.
Phase 3: Account for all, treat injuries, report and document

items.label: Abandon Ship: Mustered passengers, donned lifejackets, VHF notified, starboard gate opened, EPIRB grabbed

help.title: Abandon Ship Procedure (6 steps)
help.body:
1. Muster passengers in back, don lifejackets
2. Notify Coast Guard and nearby craft via VHF
3. Open starboard gate
4. Grab EPIRB
5. Activate EPIRB if forced or instructed by captain
6. Never abandon unless forced or instructed by captain

items.label: Flooding: Checked hatches, pumped water, closed watertight doors, fire buckets ready, passengers seated evenly

help.title: Flooding Procedure (6 steps)
help.body:
1. Check hatches and openings, pump water
2. Close watertight hatches, dog down, close machine space doors
3. Locate fire buckets as secondary water removal
4. Keep passengers seated and evenly distributed
5. Don lifejackets if conditions worsen
6. Prepare distress call
